name: Original-Cube Pruning Has a Canonical Kernel but Does Not Recognize Peelings
statement: For a finite family $H$ and protected set $A\subseteq H$, repeatedly delete an unprotected vertex whenever the cube on its current incident directions is contained in the original $H$. The terminal set $K_A(H)$ is independent of all choices. It is the greatest $U$, with $A\subseteq U\subseteq H$, such that every unprotected $v\in U$ has a set $P$ of current incident directions with $v^P\notin H$; $P$ may be chosen inclusion-minimal, so all its proper subfaces occur in $H$. A corner peeling of ample $H$ to $A$ implies $K_A(H)=A$, but the converse fails for a singleton and for the empty set: a $292$-concept rooted factor has singleton kernel at its root, and a $583$-concept ample forbidden pc-minor has empty kernel. Both have VC dimension four, in dimensions twelve and twenty-four.
proof: The deletion predicate persists because later deletions only shrink a vertex's incident support. Any set in which every unprotected vertex has an original missing-cube witness survives every allowed sequence: at its first deletion all witnessing neighbors would still be present, contradicting the predicate. The terminal set itself has such witnesses, proving it is the unique greatest fixed set. If a genuine corner peeling to $A$ existed while the kernel had an extra vertex, the first deleted kernel vertex would still have all witness neighbors, while the completing vertex was absent already in $H$, contradicting its being a corner. In the rooted counterexample the pruning begins by deleting $32$ and then $64$ because the latter's original four-cube is complete, although deleting $32$ has made that cube incomplete; this forgotten new hole explains the false positive. Certified sequences leave the stated kernels, while independent complete deletion graphs prove that the corresponding actual peelings fail.
